blurb: Rare American cat with a springy, wiry coat and crinkly whiskers
description: The American Wirehair is a rare cat breed from upstate New York, a sturdy American Shorthair relative with a springy wiry coat and a gentle, even temperament.
answer: The American Wirehair is a domestic cat breed from upstate New York, United States, defined by a wiry coat caused by a dominant mutation. It is a moderate, sturdy cat much like the American Shorthair, usually described as gentle, quiet and playful.

body: The breed began as a spontaneous mutation in a litter of five kittens born to barn cats in Vernon, New York, in 1966. A single red-and-white male had wiry fur. Rex breeder Joan O'Shea acquired him, named Adam, along with a normal-coated littermate, Tip-Top, to start a breeding program. The mutation proved different from the rex genes of the Cornish and Devon Rex. The CFA recognized the breed in 1967 and accepted it for championship in 1978; as of 2017 it was ranked the rarest of the CFA's 41 breeds. Cats were exported to Canada and Germany.

Apart from its coat, the American Wirehair resembles the American Shorthair: a moderate, sturdy build, round head, high cheekbones and a pronounced muzzle, with females generally smaller than males. The coat, ear fur and whiskers are springy and wiry, compared to the coats of wire-haired terriers. Almost all coat colors occur, though Himalayan, chocolate and lilac are not accepted for showing. Eyes are green or golden, while some white cats have blue or amber eyes. Coat quality carries 45 of 100 points in judging.

The breed's temperament is commonly described as even and balanced, essentially the same as the American Shorthair's. Wirehairs are said to be gentle and quiet-voiced yet playful and active, equally happy to play or doze in an owner's lap.
The wiry coat is reported to need little grooming. Lighter-colored cats may need sun protection. Beyond that, general cat care such as play and regular veterinary check-ups applies.
The source material does not name breed-specific health conditions. Breed clubs recommend health screening of breeding stock and regular veterinary check-ups.

faq.a: Yes. As of 2017 it was ranked the rarest of the 41 breeds recognized by the Cat Fanciers' Association.

faq.q: Does an American Wirehair need much grooming?
faq.a: The wiry coat is reported to need little grooming, although lighter-colored cats may need protection from the sun.

faq.q: Is the wirehair coat gene dominant?
faq.a: Yes. The wirehair trait is dominant, so a cross between a Wirehair and another cat can produce wire-coated kittens.
